statements.impact_statement: NVD's own CPE record for this CVE carries no version constraint at all (grype reports 'versionConstraint: none (unknown)'), so it matches every ClamAV version that has ever existed, including current upstream 1.5.4 - it cannot be cleared by any version bump. The advisory describes a 2016 denial-of-service in Cisco's AMP integration on ESA/WSA appliances ('crafted document' causing 'AMP process restart'), a Cisco-specific integration this image does not contain; nothing in this build's own code traces to it.
statements.action_statement: Re-evaluate if NVD ever publishes a version-bounded correction to this CPE record, or if a future advisory ties this CVE to code that does exist in this image.

statements.impact_statement: The vulnerable path is zlib's gz_vacate(), reached only through gzwrite()/gzprintf()/gzvprintf() while using a non-blocking, caller-managed output buffer after a write stall - confirmed against the published NVD description, not assumed from the CVE id. Every call site of that function family in ClamAV 1.4.6's own source (grep across the full tree) is a single function, tar_addfile() in common/tar.c, called only from sigtool (not installed in this image) and freshclam's own database-mirroring code in libfreshclam_internal.c, packaging freshclam's own local files - never attacker-supplied bytes, and never through clamd's scan path. That one caller also uses plain blocking gzwrite(), not the non-blocking pattern the CVE requires. This differs from app/Dockerfile's zlib VEX (CONTROL there: the code path was reachable and the fix is a verified upstream-patched build); here the call graph itself never reaches the vulnerable function, so no rebuild was made - see D-43.
statements.action_statement: Re-run this trace against any future ClamAV version bump before renewing this statement - a new release could add a caller of the gzwrite family that this analysis did not see.
